cards.explanation: The answer is judge. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), says let no one judge you by what you eat or drink. He even adds a feast, a New Moon or a Sabbath to the list. So friends, when somebody squints at your plate, you may keep right on chewing.

The answer is True. Paul, who wrote this letter (Colossians 1:1), puts a Sabbath on the list right beside a feast and a New Moon. His words are, “Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.” That's a whole list, friends, and not one seat on it for a scorekeeper.

The answer is Christ. Paul says food, drink, feasts, New Moons and Sabbaths are a shadow of the things to come, and then says “…the body that casts it belongs to Christ.” A shadow tells you something real is standing nearby. Friends, you don't hug the shadow when the real One is right there.

The answer is disqualify. Paul says not to let the person who delights in false humility and the worship of angels disqualify you with speculation about what he has seen. Speculation is just guessing, friends. A guess shouldn't get to bench anybody.

The answer is False. The verse says, “Such a person is puffed up without basis by his unspiritual mind.” So Paul calls the mind unspiritual, and he says the puffing up has no basis. Friends, that's a lot of puff with nothing underneath.

The answer is the head. Paul says, “He has lost connection to the head…” and the head is where the whole body gets its support. Elsewhere Paul writes that Christ is the head of the body, the church (Colossians 1:18). Cut off from the head, friends, nothing else is going to work.

The answer is God. Paul says the whole body is supported and knit together, and it “…grows as God causes it to grow.” The joints and ligaments do their part, but the growing is God's doing. Friends, that takes the pressure right off.

The answer is regulations. Paul asks, “…why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you submit to its regulations…” after dying with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world. That's a pointed question, friends. And the very next verse shows the kind of rules he means.

The answer is perish. After quoting “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” Paul says, “These will all perish with use…” Then he gives the reason: “…because they are based on human commands and teachings.” That's straight from the verse, friends.

The answer is human commands and teachings. Paul says the world's rules will perish with use, “…because they are based on human commands and teachings.” That's where they come from, friends. People made them up, and that's a shaky place to build from.

The answer is False. Paul says these restrictions have an appearance of wisdom, “but they are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.” Self-prescribed worship, false humility and harsh treatment of the body might look impressive. Friends, looking wise and being wise are two different things.
